draft.title: How context shapes representation
card: Context is the time, place and culture a text comes from. Representation is the way a text shows individuals, groups and places.
An author writes from within a context. Its beliefs, events and values can shape who is shown, how they are shown and what is left out.
To evaluate a representation, ask when and where the text was made, who it was made for, and how that may have shaped the picture it gives.
Example: a story from the 1800s may show a servant as humble and silent because of the class attitudes of its time. A modern story may show a servant as clever and outspoken.
draft.remember: A text's picture of people and places is shaped by the world its author lived in.

a.q: A novel written in 1890 shows factory workers as dull and unable to think for themselves. What is the best way to evaluate this representation?
opts: Ask how class attitudes of the 1890s may have shaped it
Decide that all factory workers in 1890 were dull
Decide the author must have disliked factories
Ignore it, because the novel is made up
a.why: Evaluating a representation means linking it to the time and culture the text came from, such as attitudes to class. Treating it as a true record of all workers is tempting, but it only shows how one author saw them.
a.clue: Link the picture to the author's world.

b.q: Two stories are about the same small farming town. One was written in 1920 by a landowner. One was written in 2015 by a farm worker's grandchild. Their towns differ. What best explains this?
opts: Each author's time and place shaped what they showed
One author must have lied about the town
The older story is always more accurate
Stories about a town should show it the same way
b.why: The authors come from different times and social positions, so they may notice and value different things. The older story is not more accurate just because it is older. Its picture is shaped by its own context, as the newer one is.
b.clue: Think about who wrote each story and when.

a.best: Ask how class attitudes of the 1890s may have shaped it

b.best: Each author's time and place shaped what they showed

proposal.title: How context shapes representation
card: Context is the time, place and culture a text comes from. Representation is the way a text shows individuals, groups and places.
An author writes from within a context. Its beliefs, events and values can shape who is shown, how they are shown and what is left out.
So a representation is one view, not a neutral record, even in fiction. To evaluate it, ask when and where the text was made, who it was for, and how that may have shaped it.
Example: a story from the 1800s may show a servant as humble and silent because of the class attitudes of its time. A modern story may show a servant as clever and outspoken.
proposal.remember: The world an author lives in can shape how their text shows people and places.

a.q: A novel written in 1890 shows factory workers as dull and unable to think for themselves. Which is the best evaluation of this representation?
opts: It may reflect class attitudes held in the 1890s
It may be a fair record of how workers really were
It may be unimportant, since the novel is made up
It may tell us mainly about modern views of workers
a.why: Attitudes to class in the 1890s can shape how an author of that time shows workers. Reading the novel as a fair record is tempting, but a representation is one view, not a neutral record. Being fiction does not stop it being shaped by its context.
a.clue: A novel gives a view of people, not a record of them.

b.q: Two stories are about the same small farming town. One was written in 1920 by a landowner. One was written in 2015 by a farm worker's grandchild. Their towns differ. What best explains this?
opts: Each author's time and social position shaped their view
The older story is more accurate because it came first
The newer story is more accurate because it came later
Made-up stories like these are not shaped by context
b.why: The authors come from different times and social positions, so they may notice and value different things. Neither story is more accurate just because of when it was written. Each is one view, shaped by its own context.
b.clue: Think about who wrote each story and when.

a.best: It may reflect class attitudes held in the 1890s

b.best: Each author's time and social position shaped their view
